tensor_ops.crossover_vs_shader_alu: shader ALU faster for FP8 T <= 4 and NVFP4 T <= 2; accelerator faster from FP8 T ~ 5-8 (186 vs 76 GB/s at T = 8) and NVFP4 T ~ 3 (119 GB/s at TM = 8 vs 102 at shader T = 4)

sharing.inside_dispatch: sometimes: 2 of 12 trials every foreign dispatch got in at 0.2-0.4 ms; 5 of 12 the first one waited the whole ~1.1 s; 5 of 12 a later one waited 0.5-1.0 s
sharing.typical_behind_short_dispatches: one whole command buffer: 1.04-1.05 s behind an 800-dispatch buffer in 3 of 4 runs (8 dispatches got in first in the other)

overlap.rule: encode the ALU-bound sibling before the bus-bound op

engine.note: normalized values the compiler reads (Profile.from_dict); cost_T = pass cost relative to a T = 1 pass, from p13 (shader ALUs, best geometry) and gemm_tile (#50, the cooperative-fill accelerator path, TM = 8 / 16 / 32; p14's staged tile was 1.49 / - / 1.74 and 1.53 / - / 1.78)
engine.cost_T_note: shader-FMA kernels (p13); a SIMD-group-matrix verify kernel is expected to bring T=2-4 to ~1.05-1.15 (MLX qmm_t reaches 85-91 % of nominal at T=2-4 on this chip) - re-measure when it exists
engine.accelerator_note: gemm_tile (#50/#51): at 17408x5120 the tile at TM = 8 costs 1.03 (NVFP4) / 1.09 (FP8) of a T = 1 shader pass against the shader's 1.28 / 1.08 at T = 2 and 1.79 / 1.11 at T = 4, so every format's T > 1 GEMVs take the tile (min_t 2); the shader keeps T = 1
